stem: When counseling a transplant candidate about long-term skin-cancer risk, which exposure-related factor aligns with standard references?

options.text: Cumulative sun exposure never influences post-transplant skin-cancer risk
Only a single day of sun exposure determines lifetime skin-cancer risk
Sun exposure is relevant only before birth and not after transplantation

explanation.rationale_correct: Skin-cancer risk factors in transplant recipients include cumulative exposure to sun, along with skin type, older age at transplant, immunosuppression intensity, and transplant type.

rationale_incorrect.B: Cumulative sun exposure is specifically listed as a risk factor rather than having no influence.
rationale_incorrect.C: Risk reflects cumulative exposure over time rather than a single exposure day alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Sun exposure before and after transplantation contributes to cumulative risk.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 6, Noninfectious Diseases → skin cancer → Risk factors → ii.

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 6 → skin cancer → Risk factors → ii. (cumulative sun exposure); PDF p. 280 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Cumulative-sun-exposure risk angle distinct from Fitzpatrick skin-type item (cctc-2153) and heart/lung incidence counseling (cctc-2108); anchor verified on Cupples p. 280.

stem: During pretransplant evaluation teaching about skin malignancy risk, which history-related factor aligns with standard references?

options.text: A single transplant with no retransplantation eliminates all skin-cancer risk
Retransplantation lowers skin-cancer risk compared with first transplant alone
Retransplantation affects only infectious risk, not malignancy risk

explanation.rationale_correct: Skin-cancer risk factors include retransplantation, cumulative sun exposure, immunosuppression intensity, and transplant type, among other history and host factors.

rationale_incorrect.B: Retransplantation is listed as a risk factor rather than eliminating skin-cancer risk.
rationale_incorrect.C: Retransplantation is cited as increasing risk context rather than lowering it.
rationale_incorrect.D: Retransplantation is among malignancy risk factors rather than affecting infectious risk alone.

stem: A lung transplant candidate asks what protective clothing aligns with standard malignancy-prevention references. Which counseling point is correct?

options.text: Sleeveless tops and shorts only to maximize sun exposure
Protective clothing is discouraged because it blocks all vitamin D permanently
Only broad-brimmed hats are recommended with no other clothing guidance

explanation.rationale_correct: Sun precautions include wearing protective clothing such as broad-brimmed hats and long-sleeve shirts and pants, along with sunglasses, sun visors, and sunscreen with minimum SPF 50.

rationale_incorrect.B: Protective clothing reduces undue sun exposure rather than maximizing it.
rationale_incorrect.C: Protective clothing is recommended as part of sun precautions rather than being discouraged.
rationale_incorrect.D: Long-sleeve shirts and pants are cited in addition to hats and other sun precautions.

stem: A coordinator is updating skin-cancer risk and prevention teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Cumulative exposure to sun is a cited skin-cancer risk factor.
Retransplantation is a cited skin-cancer risk factor.
Long-sleeve shirts and pants are recommended sun precautions.
Sun precautions are unnecessary for kidney transplant recipients.

explanation.rationale_correct: Cumulative sun exposure, retransplantation, and long-sleeve protective clothing are supported. Statement IV is false because sun precautions apply to transplant recipients broadly rather than being unnecessary for kidney recipients alone.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement III is also true—long-sleeve shirts and pants are recommended protective clothing.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement IV is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement IV is false because sun precautions are part of cancer prevention for all organ recipients.
